issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Pneumatic.raisePressure(pressureIncrease: int): void, but the solution implementation declares raisePressure(double pressureIncrease). This parameter-type mismatch between specification and solution will confuse students about the required signature and may cause tests or implementations to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic.raisePressure method signature consistent across artifacts. Preferably change the solution (and template) to declare void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease) to match the UML and problem statement, or alternatively update the UML/problem statement to specify a double parameter if that was intended. Ensure template, problem text, and solution use the exact same parameter type.

issues.description: The problem statement's UML declares Pneumatic.raisePressure(pressureIncrease: int) but the solution repository is inconsistent: Pneumatic interface declares raisePressure(double pressureIncrease) while the implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster) declare raisePressure(int pressureIncrease). This mismatch between the UML/problem, the interface, and the implementing classes creates a mapping and compilation confusion for students (they cannot reliably map the UML requirement to the code and the codebase itself is inconsistent).
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the raisePressure signature across all artifacts. Either change the Pneumatic interface's method to accept int (void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease)) to match the UML/problem and implementing classes, or update the UML/problem and all implementing classes to use double consistently. Ensure the template, interface, and all implementations use the identical parameter type and name so students can clearly map the UML to the code.
